## WP5: prime-power-consistent modified-prime crossing — CERTIFIED FINITE

Prior run: [38314042187](https://github.com/HMarcusWH/zeta-23-lean/actions/runs/38314042187), job 115026330098; output artifact \`post287-wp5-modified-prime\`. The 256-bit Arb job returned all of these as true:

- Modified even-sector K2 energy positive at rational L=259/200=1.295.
- Modified even-sector K2 energy negative at rational L=162/125=1.296.
- Modified odd-sector K2 energy positive **at those two endpoints**.
- Genuine-zeta even-sector K2 energy positive **at those two endpoints**.
- Both apertures lie in the same fixed prime cutoff Q=3 cell.

The model changes positive coefficients at primes 2 and 3; its prescribed prime-power coefficient at q=4 is the p=2 coefficient divided by sqrt(2), though q=4 does not enter the tested Q=3 cutoff. Pole, archimedean term, diagonal correction and source basis remain canonical. Scalar continuity supplies **some** modified even sign crossing between the endpoints. It does not prove a first crossing, a stationary crossing, whole-bracket odd positivity, or a genuine-zeta crossing.

**Disposition:** The generic claim "positive prime-power-consistent coefficient data plus canonical matrix mechanics prevent transverse crossing" is false. A source-specific ingredient would be required to exclude actual generated zeta states. The modified model is not a zeta-function counterexample and implies nothing about RH.

- L=69/100: rigorously **negative** Q on the shifted ray.

This falsifies the proposed unconditional nonnegative-Q sign throughout the admissible K2 negative-shifted ray class. It does not test the actual selected negative ground of #247, and therefore does not refute a stronger theorem with genuinely selected-state hypotheses.

**Implication:** A future sign discriminator must use more than the shifted-resolvent identity and the scalar F04 formula, and must survive the matched selected-state and non-zeta controls. No numerical sign is extrapolated to untested apertures.
